subject: Co-op Incentive & Lead Stacking for Embedded Connector Pilot
messages:
From: Emily Torres <etorres@catalystlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@consultus.io>, partnership@catalystlabs.com
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot proposal — embedded connector, revenue share & lead registry

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the connector looks promising and our engineering leads are comfortable with a narrow-scope pilot for Q4. We pulled together an initial commercial ask so we can move to an MOU quickly and align internal stakeholders. High level:

- Pilot scope: 3 customers (Catalyst-led sales) integrating Redwood’s embedding API into our Insights product; 3-month pilot.
- Commercial: 20% revenue share on direct Catalyst-led transactions for first 12 months following pilot conversion; escalating to 25% if ARR > $150k within 12 months.
- Lead registration: 180-day exclusivity window for registered leads, with Catalyst required to provide source evidence (email thread or CRM record).
- Trial credits: $10k platform credit to cover usage during pilot; request convertible to a one-time implementation credit on first invoice.
- Co-marketing: small MDF of $7k for joint webinar + 1 case study.

Attached is a short draft (Catalyst_RevShare_Draft_v1.pdf) and a sample lead registry template (MOP_Lead_Registry_Template.xlsx).

Two quick asks: can Redwood accept the 20/25 tiered rev-share? And can you confirm the lead registration evidence you require so we can instrument handoffs in our CRM?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful — Tom and I are flexible next week.

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of Partnerships, Catalyst Labs
etorres@catalystlabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0172


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — embedded connector, revenue share & lead registry

Emily —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the materials. High-level reactions from our side:

- Rev-share: 20% for first 12 months is reasonable for a first-of-a-kind embed pilot; the 25% kicker is okay, but we prefer a performance trigger tied to net new ARR (we'll propose ARR > $150k net new to Redwood).
- Lead registration: we can do a 120-day registration window instead of 180; we require CRM export evidence (HubSpot lead record + email thread or signed SOW). We also ask that Catalyst not reassign or repurpose the lead to a competing partner during the registration window.
- Trial credits: we can approve a $10k credit for usage. The credit will be applied to invoice as a one-time implementation credit on first paid invoice after pilot conversion; non-converted pilots forfeit the credit.
- MDF: Redwood can support a co-marketing fund of up to $5k for joint events; if Catalyst can top up the remainder we can proceed.

Operational asks: can you use our standard lead registry spreadsheet (I attached our version in a shared doc link) and supply contact person + timestamped intro email for each registered lead? We need to confirm that each registered lead is an introduction — warm intro or direct handoff — not a lead sourced independently by Catalyst marketing.

Ben, Laura — tagging for SR and commercial review. Can you review the revenue share math and confirm whether the 120-day registration is operationally enforceable from our side?

If this looks okay, I'll draft a short MOU to capture the pilot terms and then loop Legal for a light SOW and rev-share clause. We can do a 30-min sync next Tue (12th) afternoon.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Emily Torres <etorres@catalystlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Aug 2025 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — embedded connector, revenue share & lead registry

Soojin / Emily —

Quick commercial math and a few risk points:

- The 20% rev-share on Catalyst-led transactions is straightforward. For bookkeeping, we will net usage and apply the rev-share monthly once invoices clear. We need Catalyst to provide transaction-level reporting (invoice number, customer name, date, gross invoice amount) within 30 days of month-end for reconciliation.
- Escalator to 25%: to avoid gaming, we'll require the ARR trigger to be measured on Redwood-recognized revenue only (new Redwood ARR attributable to Catalyst introductions).
- Lead registration window: 120 days is fine. Add an exception for inbound accounts where Catalyst can provide the first meaningful touch evidence (email intro or meeting invite) — that will qualify as registration.
- Exclusivity: we cannot offer territory or vertical exclusivity for Catalyst, but we can agree to lead-level protection as described.

Operational proposal: I attached a short reconciliation cadence to this thread (see MOP_Lead_Registry_Template.xlsx) — monthly reporting and quarterly settlement. If Catalyst agrees, I'll include the reporting cadence in the MOU.

One open commercial ask from our revenue team: if a converted customer churns within 90 days, Redwood requests a pro-rata clawback of rev-share payments contributed to Catalyst for that customer. Standard practice for pilot-driven conversions.

Happy to join the call next Tue and finalize MOU language.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Partnerships Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Emily Torres <etorres@catalystlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@consultus.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — embedded connector, revenue share & lead registry

Soojin / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turn. We discussed internally and the summary below captures our acceptance with two small redlines:

1) Trail period --> 180 days lead registration: Catalyst will accept 120 days if Redwood will make a one-time exception to extend a single strategic account to 180 days (we'll identify which account at the time of registration).
2) Clawback: We accept a pro-rata clawback on churn within 90 days but ask that the calculation be based on net new ARR (same measurement as the escalator) and that clawbacks be limited to payments made within the first 180 days after conversion.

We can accept the MDF split (Catalyst covers the $2k incremental). Doc: I've uploaded a signed-commented draft to Google Docs and requested a DocuSign route for a one-page MOU (link in related_links).

Next steps we propose:
- Soojin to send a 1-page MOU capturing the pilot scope, rev-share tiers, lead registration rules, trial credit treatment, MDF split, reporting cadence, and the clawback language.
- Emily to populate the MOP lead registry with initial 3 prospects and provide timestamped intros.
- Ben to confirm settlement cadence and template in the MOU.

We'll be ready to start engineering discovery week of Aug 25 pending the MOU.

Talk soon — Emily

Emily Torres
Head of Partnerships | Catalyst Labs
etorres@catalystlabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: Catalyst_RevShare_Draft_v1.pdf, MOP_Lead_Registry_Template.xlsx
